candidates.name: PROJECT PLUTO / SLAM
candidates.caption: A cruise missile powered by a nuclear ramjet. The engine ran; the proposed weapon never took flight.
candidates.why_unbuilt: The Pentagon reconsidered its sponsorship and Project Pluto was cancelled on 1 July 1964.
candidates.what_remains: Official histories, test photographs, and technical records document the Tory nuclear ramjet engines.
candidates.note: Candidate scope is the proposed flight weapon, not the engine: Tory reactors and a flight-engine prototype were built and tested. NNSS gives 1 January 1957 and 1 July 1964 dates; LLNL confirms successful ground tests. Verify the exact SLAM airframe designation and flight-vehicle completion status before promotion. Do not write 'no prototype was built' or suggest that reactor tests failed. Avoid unsupported fallout-casualty numbers or claims about deliberate radiation trails.

candidates.name: SWISSMETRO
candidates.caption: A fast train beneath Switzerland. The network remained a promise beneath the timetable.
candidates.why_unbuilt: The original company lacked continued political and economic support and proposed liquidation in 2009.
candidates.what_remains: The 1994–1998 main-study report preserves the proposed maglev system, tunnels, stations and network.
candidates.note: *1992 marks the original company's formation; the idea originated earlier in the 1970s. Scope is the original Swissmetro SA project, not SwissMetro-NG or later Hyperloop proposals. The main-study report was issued on 31 May 1999 and describes reduced-pressure underground tunnels and magnetic levitation. It proposed future construction, not a completed network. The 2 November 2009 news account reports proposed liquidation; verify final legal dates before promotion. Design feasibility and profitability were study claims, not independently demonstrated outcomes.

candidates.why_unbuilt: Constellation was cancelled in 2010; NASA subsequently replaced Ares V with the Space Launch System.

candidates.note: *2005 dates the initiation of Ares V; the endpoint spans Constellation's 2010 cancellation and the September 2011 SLS replacement, which this NASA-authored 2015 paper dates as Ares V's cancellation. Related engine/component work existed; no claim that no hardware of any kind was built. Before promotion verify final integrated-vehicle completion status and choose a specific configuration. No single budget or technical cause is inferred.

candidates.name: LOCKHEED L-2000
candidates.caption: A rival American supersonic airliner. The competition chose Boeing; Lockheed stayed on the ground.
candidates.why_unbuilt: Lockheed lost the US supersonic-transport design competition to Boeing in 1966.
candidates.what_remains: A Smithsonian wind-tunnel model and NASA histories preserve the proposed supersonic transport.
candidates.source_name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
candidates.note: *1966 marks the competition decision, not the first design study. The Smithsonian search record explicitly identifies Lockheed’s loss to Boeing; full page retrieval returned 403. NASA’s Contributions to Aeronautics, vol. 2, pp. 591–592, independently confirms selection on the last day of 1966, the competing Model 2000 design, and full-scale mock-ups as the only aircraft built. Do not conflate this decision with cancellation of the overall US SST programme in 1971. Wind-tunnel models and a mock-up existed: do not claim no hardware was built. Full-size mock-up configuration and exact early chronology require further review before promotion.

Configurations evolved; technology pre-development and concept models are not completed flight spacecraft or an operational Darwin observatory.
